concern_results.conclusion: Removing terminal emphasis and checking terminal punctuation once both match the tests. The empty-emphasis and malformed-marker indexing paths cannot go out of range. Labelled stops recheck without a delivery-eligibility check, but the tests intend this, so it is not blocking.

The hook only returns a block reason, bounded by stop_hook_active. The reason text keeps the safety blockers and grants no authority. The session-policy commit/push/merge wording now matches the goal-authorization rule in the root AGENTS.md.

Scanning a long line without a question mark skips the question regex. The remaining regexes are anchored or bounded ({0,40}), so the scan stays linear. Truncated transcripts fall back to recent-context edit evidence.

The tests cover positive, negative, quoted, emphasized, Chinese and long-line cases. The long-line case runs as a subprocess with a 5-second timeout, so it would fail on the old quadratic scan. The evidence reports 14 failures on the base matcher.

The hook payload and entrypoint are unchanged. Refactoring handoff() into prose_lines/handoff_values keeps the earlier behavior. Two base-quiet cases (blocked/awaiting) were intentionally reclassified and documented.
No state or migration. Reverting the matcher is enough; the npm version bump is consistent across both files.
The 'Decision recheck' reason string is the observable result. No new logging is needed.
The plan says outright that the native-payload checks are synthetic and do not prove model follow-through. The review-lane-status file admits independent review is outstanding.
This is a shared-gate hook. The one-retry bound is preserved, and no path executes transcript content or grants merge or credential authority.
